issues.description: Hard dependency on opentelemetry private API _logs.LoggingHandler scattered in three places
issues.detail: You're importing from opentelemetry.sdk._logs (underscore = private) in _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry, then doing isinstance scans over root.handlers. Three copies of the same handler-discovery hack. Wrap it in one helper that returns the OTLP handler, and accept that you're coupled to a private API — at least centralize the breakage point.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: log buffering, worker race fix, and makefile/test changes mashed into one PR
issues.detail: The actual feature is crash-log upload. The worker.py reorder (queue_msg before pending_assignments registration) is a separate race-condition fix. The makefile change removing -n auto and dropping test_plugin_google_stt is a third unrelated change. Bisecting a regression here is hostile to whoever inherits this. Split it.

issues.description: Removing -n auto from unit tests silently kills parallel test execution with no justification
issues.detail: The commit message says nothing about why parallel test execution is being dropped, or why test_plugin_google_stt is being removed from the suite. CI will get slower and that test stops running. Either it's flaky — say so in the commit — or this is a debugging artifact that snuck in. Either way, not acceptable unexplained.

issues.description: _BufferingHandler has unbounded memory growth with no cap
issues.detail: If session.start() is slow or never reached and the process logs heavily, buffer grows without limit until _on_cleanup runs. For a crash-log path specifically this is mostly fine, but a misbehaving job that spams logs pre-connect can OOM the worker. Add a cap (ring buffer or max records) — this is exactly the kind of unbounded list a maintainer will curse later.

issues.description: Bare `except Exception` in _on_cleanup swallows everything from init_recording
issues.detail: The fallback init_recording call catches Exception broadly and logs it. Fine for a cleanup path, but at minimum narrow it or log which RecordingOptions field failed. As written, an ImportError from the voice module looks identical to a real telemetry setup failure.

issues.description: Local import of RecordingOptions inside _on_cleanup hides a real circular-import problem
issues.detail: `from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions` inside the function body is the usual tell that job.py and voice/agent_session.py have a cycle. Top-of-file import would be cleaner; if you can't, leave a one-line comment saying why. Otherwise the next reader has to reproduce the import error to figure it out.

review.summary: The core idea — buffer logs early, flush them on crash via OTLP — is reasonable and solves a real operational problem. The implementation is messy: it reaches into opentelemetry private API (_logs.LoggingHandler) and does handler-list isinstance scans in two separate places, which is the kind of thing that breaks silently on an upstream version bump. The PR also bundles three unrelated changes (the log feature, a worker.py race fix, and a makefile change that disables parallel tests and drops a test file with no justification) — that's THREE-PATCHES, not one. Buffer has no size cap. NEEDS-WORK: split the PR, centralize the OTLP handler lookup, explain the makefile change, and cap the buffer.
